candidates.change_summary: Replace withdraw(address(this).balance) with revert() so withdrawAll no longer transfers funds, changing the balance-dependent behavior.
Delete the withdraw call inside withdrawAll so the function does nothing, leaving the contract balance unchanged.
Replace require(msg.sender == owner) with require(false) so onlyOwner always reverts, preventing withdrawAll from executing.
Remove the require statement from the onlyOwner modifier, making it do nothing.
Replace the transfer call with a no-op by removing the entire body of withdraw function.
Change the recipient of transfer to a zero address, effectively burning the funds.
Replace transfer with a call to sendMoney to owner, which could revert on failure instead of automatically reverting.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from withdraw, allowing anyone to call it.

Remove the if-revert on call failure so sendMoney does not revert on failed _target.call, yet _s is unused, changing caller’s external view of success/failure and subsequent state (note: the target behavior is sendMoney value; without revert, call can fail silently and depositsCount/balance may differ after sendMoney returns).

Replace the low-level call with a transfer (which reverts on failure with a different gas stipend), so sendMoney behavior changes for a call that would have failed silently or with different error handling.
Delete the entire sendMoney body (make it a no-op), so no value is ever sent and the state visible via subsequent calls differs.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from sendMoney so anyone can call it, changing who can trigger value transfers and thus affecting contract balance and depositsCount visible to the owner.
Change the require in onlyOwner to always pass (remove the condition), granting anyone access to sendMoney and thus altering when value can be sent.
